title: Tens and ones: numbers to 100
summary: Bundle ten ones into a ten. Build and read numbers to 100 with tens and ones.
guide: This studio is for Year 1. The sentences are short; read them aloud if your child can't read yet. The picture above each mission shows which button to press.
Each column is a place: the ones on the right, the tens on the left. Under each column, the place-value chart shows that column's digit.
The ← 10 button bundles ten ones into one ten. The 1 → button breaks a ten into ten ones. The number stays the same; only the way it is made changes.
If a column holds 10 or more, its digit turns red: only one digit fits in each place. So it's time to exchange.
Use the buttons above the picture to switch to the {{term:abacus}}, which shows the same thing with beads.

make-a-ten.title: Make a ten
make-a-ten.prompt: Here are 14 ones. Bundle ten of them into a ten.
make-a-ten.hint: Ten ones have a dotted ring. Press ← 10.
make-a-ten.success: Well done! 1 ten and 4 ones. That's 14.
make-a-ten.why: You had 14 ones. Now you have 1 ten and 4 ones. Which is more? Why?
make-a-ten.model: Neither. Both are 14. We only bundled ten ones together. One ten is the same as ten ones.

feedback.needs-exchange: There are still 10 ones together. Press ← 10.
feedback.too-big: You added some. It should stay 14. Just bundle.
feedback.too-small: You took some away. It should stay 14. Just bundle.
feedback.empty: You took them all away! Put 14 ones back.

read-the-number.title: Count and write
read-the-number.prompt: How many tens? How many ones? Write the number.
read-the-number.hint: Count the tens first: 10, 20, 30, … Then count the ones.
read-the-number.success: Well done! 4 tens and 7 ones make 47.
read-the-number.model: The 4 means 4 tens. That's 40. The 7 means 7 ones.

feedback.reversed: You swapped the digits. The tens digit comes first, on the left.
feedback.added-digits: You added 4 and 7. Each ten is ten ones. Count the tens in tens.
feedback.too-big: Too many. Count the tens again.
feedback.too-small: Too few. Each ten is ten. Count in tens.
feedback.empty: Write the number in the box.

add-tens.title: Add tens
add-tens.prompt: You have 25. Add 3 tens. Guess first: what will it be?
add-tens.hint: Press + under the tens three times. The ones don't change.
add-tens.why: 25 became 55. Which digit changed? Why didn't the other one?
add-tens.model: The tens digit went from 2 to 5, because we added 3 tens. The ones stayed 5, because we didn't add any ones.

feedback.added-ones: You added 3 ones. Add 3 tens. Press + under the tens.
feedback.too-small: Not enough yet. You need 3 tens.
feedback.needs-exchange: There are 10 ones together. Make a ten first.

break-a-ten.title: Break a ten
break-a-ten.prompt: You have 32. Take away 5 ones. There are only 2 ones! What can you do?
break-a-ten.hint: Press 1 →. A ten opens into ten ones. Then take away 5.
break-a-ten.success: Well done! You broke a ten and took 5 away. 27 is left.
break-a-ten.why: Why did you have to break a ten first?
break-a-ten.model: There were only 2 ones, so I couldn't take 5. I broke a ten and had 12 ones. I took 5 away: 7 ones and 2 tens are left. That's 27.

feedback.only-two: You took 2. Take 3 more. First break a ten with 1 →.
feedback.took-ten: You took a whole ten: that's 10! We only want 5. Put the ten back and break it.
feedback.took-tens: You took tens. We only want 5 ones.
feedback.too-big: You haven't taken 5 away yet. Take ones with −.
feedback.too-small: You took too many. Just 5 ones.
feedback.needs-exchange: There are 10 ones together. Bundle them back into a ten.
